title: Фирменный омлет и звонок мамы  (The Signature Omelet and Mom's Call)

segments.t: In the apartment kitchen, Kostya proudly serves Nastya his signature omelet just before her mother calls once again to ask when they are getting married. Meanwhile at Claude Monet, Ainura complains about the latest kitchen fines by joking about swatting a moth.
Я вчера в шкаф умолю била.
Мне теперь за нее тоже деньги дать, да?
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'My signature omelet.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'signature' and finishing on 'omelette'.
'I only looked away for a second.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'to show' places the action in the masculine past tense. Sasha answers right away.
'Who is that?' The grammar packs 'this' and 'who' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Give me two thousand rubles.' Notice how Russian expresses 'give' and 'thousands' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Two thousand rubles.' Kostya anchors the line on 'two', while 'thousands' completes the thought. Sasha answers right away.
'Who called?' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'called' places the action in the masculine past tense.
'My mom called.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'mum' before landing on 'called'.
'Once again she wanted to ask about the wedding.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'another' and finishing on 'to ask'. Sasha answers right away.
'Well, I will call her back later.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'come on' and finishing on 'will call back'.
'Is everything alright?' Max anchors the line on 'all', while 'fine' completes the thought.
'Look, just look at this.' The meaning hinges on 'look' working together with 'look' in spoken Russian. Sasha answers right away.
Я вчера в шкаф умолю била.
'Yesterday I killed a moth in the closet.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'to beat' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Мне теперь за нее тоже деньги дать, да?
'Do I have to pay money for that moth now too?' Max brings out the contrast between 'for me' and 'now' in a few short words. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Я вчера в шкаф умолю била.
Мне теперь за нее тоже деньги дать, да?
